dateline: Hawthorne, CA / Boca Chica, TX — May 2002–Present
heroHeadline: Starship IFT-12 Block 3 Completes First V3 Flight — Raptor Relight in Space Achieved; Ship 39 Splashes Down in Indian Ocean; Booster 19 Lost; IPO Roadshow June 4–8
heroSubtitle: 8,784 days of SpaceX milestones — Starship IFT-12 Block 3 launched May 22, 2026 at 22:30 UTC from Orbital Launch Pad 2 (OLP-2) at Starbase, marking the inaugural launch from Pad 2 and the debut of the Block 3 / V3 architecture. Ship 39 (124.4 m, 25% more propellant than V2) successfully splashed down in the Indian Ocean ~65 minutes after liftoff, with the V3 heat-shield performing well under observation from two modified Starlink camera satellites. SpaceX achieved a landmark first: a single Raptor Vacuum engine was successfully relighted in space, validating a critical propulsion capability for orbital refueling and interplanetary missions. All 22 Starlink mass-simulators were deployed. However, Booster 19 suffered an off-nominal boostback burn — several Raptor 3 engines in the outer ring failed to ignite — causing a transonic ocean impact rather than the planned Gulf of Mexico splashdown. IFT-13 planning will incorporate analysis of the boostback anomaly. On May 23, Falcon 9 mission Starlink 17-37 launched from Vandenberg SLC-4E, deploying 24 more Starlink V2 Mini satellites; booster B1100 made its 6th successful landing on OCISLY (614th cumulative booster recovery). SpaceX: 62 orbital missions in 2026, 614 total booster recoveries, 10,451+ Starlink satellites in orbit, 10.3M subscribers. IPO roadshow: June 4–8; pricing June 11; Nasdaq (SPCX) debut June 12.
